thread:
Liam O'Connor: FYI running into weird failures when our python SDK talks to Dedicated via customer's VPC + proxy. intermittent TLS verify errors and occasionally an Invalid URL error when base_url has a trailing slash.

Sofia Morales: ugh, trailing slash bugs are the worst. paste a small repro? sync or async?

Liam O'Connor: async. snippet (sanitized):

Liam O'Connor: ```py
from pathlib import Path
from redwood import AsyncClient

client = AsyncClient(
    api_key='redacted',
    base_url='https://private.example/',  # note trailing slash
    proxies={'https': 'http://proxy.corp.internal:8080'},
    verify=Path('/etc/ssl/corp_root.pem')
)

async def ping():
    return await client.chat.create(messages=[{'role':'user','content':'ping'}])
```

Liam O'Connor: failures look like: CertificateVerifyError: unable to get local issuer certificate OR httpx.URLInvalidError when the SDK concatenates paths badly. only under high concurrency or when the proxy cluster returns different intermediary chains.

Ben Patel: do you see the URLInvalidError reproducible? that sounds like double-slash handling or our client joining base_url + route incorrectly. we should normalize base_url at Client init (strip trailing slash).

Sofia Morales: and the certs issue — are you passing a pathlib.Path? httpx accept verify as str | bool | SSLContext, but our wrapper might not accept Path and drop the arg silently. IDE didn't warn me either.

Liam O'Connor: exactly. I passed a Path and got no immediate error; under load it misbehaved. converting to str fixed the cert path case for me. passing an ssl.SSLContext also helped.

Ben Patel: ok action items: 1) make Client/AsyncClient constructors accept ca_bundle: str | Path | ssl.SSLContext in typing stubs, 2) coerce Path -> str internally, 3) always build one SSLContext at init if a path is provided and reuse it for all pools, 4) normalize base_url (strip trailing slash) to avoid URL join issues.

Sofia Morales: +1 on typed param. also we should add REDWOOD_CA_BUNDLE env precedence docs and clarify that explicit arg > env > system. and include a short code example showing both path and SSLContext options. developers often prefer Path objects.

Liam O'Connor: another nuance: customer proxy does TLS interception and different egress nodes present different intermediate certs. if your PEM only contains the root but misses intermediates you'll hit intermittent verification failures. bundling the full chain or using SSLContext with load_verify_locations(full_chain) is the reliable approach.

Ben Patel: created tickets: DEVEX-1601 (py-sdk: normalize base_url + fix URL join), DEVEX-1602 (py-sdk: ca_bundle typing + Path coercion + consistent SSLContext init), DEVEX-1603 (docs: Dedicated quickstart - CA bundles + proxy best practices).

Sofia Morales: small API suggestion: expose a TLSConfig dataclass in the public API that can hold ca_bundle, cert, key, verify_mode, and include pydantic-friendly schema for customers using it with config files. typed and discoverable.

Ben Patel: agree. TLSConfig dataclass would make it discoverable in IDEs and avoid ad-hoc param lists. we'll prototype in DEVEX-1602. also add integration tests: per-coro client creation (should warn or be discouraged) and proxy simulator that rotates intermediates to catch flakey certs.

Liam O'Connor: short-term workaround notes for anyone hitting this: 1) share one AsyncClient across coroutines, 2) pass a str path or pre-built ssl.SSLContext (not Path unless we coerce), 3) include full intermediate chain in the PEM when proxies intercept.

devex-bot: DEVEX-1601/1602/1603 created and linked. Assigning to @ben.patel for follow-up.
